summary: Root cause: the shared postgres 'ledger-db' ran out of disk (measured disk_used_pct 96.58% @14:20Z → ≥98% @14:38Z → pinned 100% from 14:59Z) because the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retained tens of GB of WAL (33916 MB @14:34:05Z → 77371 MB @14:49:47Z), until Postgres PANIC'd on its own pg_wal and base/ files (15:01Z) and clients surfaced verbatim 'No space left on device'. All four shared-DB writers' evidence places the origin at ledger-db, and the failure began independently of payment-service v6.0.0. Confidence 0.66 (medium, capped): the mechanism, component and fix are each directly observed, but two gaps keep it short of high — the slot's inactivity has no identified actor, and one co-writer (portfolio-service) did not degrade. v6.0.0 is coincidental: the resource trend precedes the 14:46Z deploy, the errors are physical storage errors not schema/enum rejections, and rollback at 15:12Z did not reduce errors through 16:57:54Z. The precedent-backed fix (HIST-114) is to drop/recreate the stalled slot to release retained WAL and add slot-lag/inactivity alerting.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db disk exhaustion from WAL retained by an inactive replication slot
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared postgres 'ledger-db' ran out of disk space because the replication slot 'analytics_cdc' went inactive and retained tens of GB of WAL. Write paths terminating in ledger-db began failing with 'No space left on device', surfacing as payment-service ledger write failures (~60% error rate). payment-service v6.0.0 is coincidental: the resource trend started ~12 min BEFORE the deploy, and rolling the deploy back did not clear the errors. Confidence is capped because the SHARED-db scope claim (all four writers fail together) is inferred from the shared:true flag and error text, not observed co-writer behaviour — the very query that separates this from H3 was never run.

causal_chain.claim: Replication slot 'analytics_cdc' becomes inactive and begins retaining WAL (33916 MB by 14:34:05Z, 69518 MB by 14:46:32Z, 77371 MB by 14:49:47Z)
Retained WAL fills the ledger-db data volume; measured disk_used_pct is already 96.58% at 14:20Z, ≥98% from 14:38Z, and pinned at 100.0% from 14:59Z
Postgres PANICs: 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478: No space left on device' (15:01:01Z) and 'could not extend file base/16402/2619: No space left on device' (15:01:39Z)

Client writes terminating in ledger-db fail and are surfaced verbatim as 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' by payment-service (uniform 59/59 and 266/266 ERROR patterns; no mandate-specific or validation text)

The failing path is shared: order-service ('INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device', first 15:00:42Z) and settlement-service (error rate 54.04% in the same 15:00Z bucket) fail on the same disk signature within ~16 s / the same 3-min bucket as payment-service, while portfolio-service — a co-writer — does not degrade
Because the origin is the DB, rollback of v6.0.0 at 15:12Z does not restore payments; errors persist at ~60% through 16:57:54Z

assumptions: Retained WAL is the (dominant) consumer of ledger-db disk; the 33916→77371 MB figures are log-reported quantities, not the measured disk series (no WAL-size metric exists) — the disk_used_pct series corroborates only the consequence

Settlement-service's identical 'No space left on device' log text was never retrieved (query timed out), so its participation rests on its error-rate onset bucket plus its status as a direct ledger-db writer
The slot becoming inactive has no actor in the change data (zero deploys and zero config changes on 2026-06-01), so the true first cause of slot inactivity is unexplained

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db storage/volume-level infrastructure fault (not a retention-policy misconfiguration)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The ledger-db node, its data volume, or its WAL/I/O subsystem failed at the storage level — a genuine infrastructure fault — which happened to manifest as disk exhaustion and WAL retention. Origin is the ledger-db host/volume rather than the replication-slot retention policy, which would call for a host/volume-level fix rather than only dropping a slot.

causal_chain.claim: The ledger-db storage/WAL subsystem degrades independently beginning ~14:34Z (WAL retention warnings, then disk fills)
Measured disk_used_pct climbs 96.58%@14:20Z → 98.21%@14:38Z → 100.0%@14:59Z, consistent with either retained WAL or another volume-level consumer
Postgres PANICs on its own WAL and data files from 15:01Z
All direct writers to ledger-db fail ledger writes, including payment-service, independent of v6.0.0
Rollback of v6.0.0 fails to restore payments

assumptions: No host/volume/IOPS telemetry exists to distinguish a hardware/volume fault from a retention-policy fill (no ledger-db host metrics beyond disk_used_pct, cpu_pct, connections_active, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min were retrieved)
The WAL retention is a symptom/co-symptom rather than the primary mechanism

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unmanaged/abandoned replication-slot consumer as an unowned out-of-band change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The origin is an unowned, out-of-inventory component behind the 'analytics_cdc' slot: no service in the platform owns or consumes that slot, so whatever process stopped consuming WAL (a decommissioned CDC sink, a paused pipeline, a dead client) is the true trigger. Because no deploy or config change for any service is recorded on 2026-06-01, the change that inactivated the consumer must be out-of-band / unmanaged — which also explains why it appears nowhere in the change ledger. This is distinct from H1 (which treats the retention policy/dropped slot as the fix target) in that it names a different origin: the unmanaged consumer, and would call for ownership/monitoring remediation, not merely clearing WAL.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: analytics_cdc slot consumer (unmanaged, not in service inventory)

causal_chain.claim: An unmanaged consumer stops advancing the 'analytics_cdc' replication slot, so WAL is retained (33916 MB@14:34Z → 77371 MB@14:49Z)
No platform service owns or consumes the slot: no analytics-service or CDC/warehouse component exists, and ledger-db's depth-2 neighbourhood contains no analytics/CDC edge
The consumer's stop is not in any change record: zero deploys and zero config/flag changes for any service on 2026-06-01, including the 13:00–14:40Z window around slot inactivity onset
Retained WAL fills the volume; disk_used_pct → 100%, Postgres PANICs and ledger writes fail platform-wide
payments break downstream of the DB failure and rollback does not help

assumptions: The consumer exists outside the modelled inventory (the tooling's absence of it is an ownership/visibility gap, not proof of non-existence — F23)
An out-of-band change to that unmanaged consumer actually occurred around 14:30–14:34Z; this is unobservable with current tooling

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0's new MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type overloads or is rejected by the ledger tier
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 mandate flow writes a new ledger entry type (MANDATE_HOLD) that either causes abnormal/duplicated writes filling the shared ledger-db disk, or is rejected by ledger-db's schema/enum validation, producing ledger write failures. Origin is the release.

causal_chain.claim: v6.0.0 (dep-6203) deploys 14:46:00Z adding mandate endpoints and new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD
New mandate flow writes MANDATE_HOLD entries, causing a write surge or validation rejection
ledger-db rejects/overflows on those writes and payment-service surfaces 'ledger write failed'
Rollback at 15:12Z should have cleared it

assumptions: The new entry type actually reaches ledger-db and is validated there
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Ruled out: (a) the universal error text is a physical storage error ('could not extend file: No space left on device') and the DB PANIC'd on its own pg_wal file — not a schema/enum rejection (F8, F10); (b) zero 'mandate' log lines anywhere, so the failure is not mandate-path-specific (F9); (c) the WAL/disk trend and the measured disk_used_pct climb (already ≥98%@14:38Z per F28) start BEFORE the 14:46Z deploy (F11, F16, F28); (d) rollback at 15:12Z did not reduce errors through 16:57Z, and co-writers that never received v6.0.0 fail identically (F17, F12, F24, F25, F27). The schema-rejection arm is also unsupported (no schema-change records exist), but the physical-storage evidence is decisive regardless.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Fault in payment-service's own DB connection/resource handling (not shared DB, not mandate schema)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Something within payment-service's own ledger-write path — connection pool exhaustion, local filesystem, or write-path code — is the origin, explaining the error jump and the mandated rollback.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service resource exhaustion (pool/local fs) begins at onset
ledger write errors are emitted carrying the shared DB's 'No space left on device' text

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rejected: the 'No space left on device' errors are emitted by the shared ledger-db's own WAL and data filesystems, which PANIC'd on their own files (F10); payment-service has no local filesystem or pool evidence; and rollback did not change error rates (F17) while co-writers order-service and settlement-service show the same failure (F24, F25).

facts.statement: The failing component is the shared postgres database 'ledger-db' (there is no service named 'ledger-service'), which showed WARN 'disk usage 98% on /var/lib/postgresql/data' at 14:48:20Z, then PANIC "could not write to file \"pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478\": No space left on device" at 15:01:01Z and 'could not extend file "base/16402/2619": No space left on device' at 15:01:39Z.

ledger-db's disk pressure came from an inactive replication slot retaining WAL, starting well before the DB errors: WARN "replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 33916 MB of WAL" at 14:34:05Z, growing to 69518 MB at 14:46:32Z and 77371 MB at 14:49:47Z.

ledger-db exposes a measured 'disk_used_pct' metric series (180 s buckets, full non-partial 51 points): 96.58% at 14:20Z, 98.21% @14:38Z, 99.08% @14:47Z, 99.72% @14:53Z, 99.95% @14:56Z, then pinned at 100.0% from 14:59Z through 15:08Z.

payment-service is a direct writer to the shared postgres ledger-db (edge kind 'db'); ledger-db is shared:true with four direct writers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
payment-service error_rate jumped from a stable ~0.2% baseline (all 14:00–14:56Z buckets ≤0.29%) to 60.15% in the 15:00:00Z bucket and stayed 59–66% through 16:56Z.

payment-service's errors are uniformly ledger write failures, not mandate-flow-specific validation rejects: 59/59 ERROR logs in 14:30–15:20Z are the single pattern 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (first at 15:00:26Z), and 266 ERROR entries in 15:30–16:59Z are the same pattern.
A log search for 'mandate' on payment-service over 14:55–15:20Z returned total_matched 0 (untruncated), so no mandate-flow-specific error signature exists — the failure is generic to ledger writes.

The shared ledger-db resource trend precedes the deploy: WAL retention was already 33916 MB at 14:34:05Z and disk hit 98% at 14:48:20Z, whereas v6.0.0 deployed at 14:46:00Z and errors began at 15:00:26Z.

Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in the 05:00–16:59Z window on 2026-06-01: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203), deployed 14:46:00Z by p.nair, status 'rolled_back' at 15:12:00Z; no other service's deploy lines up with onset.

Rollback did not clear the failure: after v6.0.0 was rolled back at 15:12:00Z, payment-service errors continued at the same ~60% rate through the last error at 16:57:54Z, still the identical ledger-db 'No space left on device' pattern.

order-service (a ledger-db co-writer) held ~0.2% error_rate through 14:56Z, then jumped to 47.78% in the 15:00:00Z bucket and stayed 47–48% through 15:08Z, with its first error 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device orderId=8ab6dc3a' at 15:00:42Z — 16 s after payment-service's first error — and 236 matched ERROR entries all of that single pattern.
settlement-service (a ledger-db co-writer) stayed ≤0.28% through 14:56Z, then jumped to 54.04% in the 15:00:00Z bucket and continued at 53.57% / 57.74% (max 58.51).
portfolio-service (also a direct ledger-db writer) did NOT degrade over 14:20–15:08Z (max error_rate 0.30%) and returned zero 'space' matches in its ERROR logs over 14:20–16:59Z (untruncated).

No config or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service on 2026-06-01 in the 05:00–16:59Z window (count 0), and the 13:00–15:00Z window around the slot-inactivation onset is also empty (count 0, partial:false).

No CDC/replication/analytics consumer exists in the platform inventory to own the 'analytics_cdc' slot (known_services contains no analytics-service and no CDC/warehouse component), and ledger-db's dependency neighbourhood (both directions, depth 2) contains no analytics/CDC consumer.

No deployment attributable to any CDC owner exists at any hour of 2026-06-01: zero deployments across all services in 00:00–05:00Z and 13:00–14:40Z (partial:false), plus no deploys other than dep-6203 at 14:46Z in 05:00–16:59Z.

HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db 'disk full from retained WAL') is the matching precedent: root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (category resource_exhaustion, symptoms 'no space left on device'/'write failures'), resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'.

No historical incident records a root cause matching 'new ledger entry type rejected'; other ledger-db precedents were infrastructure/query-side, and the only payment-service precedent found was a bank-partner API 5xx outage.

assumptions: The retained WAL from the inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot is the dominant consumer of ledger-db disk. The 33916→77371 MB figures are log-reported quantities; ledger-db exposes no WAL-size metric, and the disk_used_pct series corroborates only the consequence (disk fill), not the WAL attribution.

H1's first cause — whatever inactivated the 'analytics_cdc' slot at ~14:34Z — has no identified actor in any change plane (zero deploys, zero config/flag changes on 2026-06-01). The true trigger of slot inactivity remains unexplained; the fix targets the slot-side mechanism rather than that trigger.

settlement-service's verbatim 'No space left on device' error text was never retrieved (log query timed out 3x); its participation rests on the same onset bucket (54.04% @15:00Z) plus its status as a direct ledger-db writer, not on its own log text.

portfolio-service's flat error rate and zero 'space' matches are unexplained by a pure shared-DB-fills-up story (e.g. different code path, retries, or non-disk write path), and its health was not verified through end-of-window.

The shared-DB scope claim (all four writers fail together) is supported for two of the three non-payment writers (order-service, settlement-service) at the same onset bucket; the fourth (portfolio-service) did not fail, so 'all four writers fail together' holds only approximately.

ledger-db host/volume-level health beyond disk_used_pct (IOPS, filesystem, hardware) was not measured, so a storage-level fault co-manifesting with the disk exhaustion cannot be fully excluded (H3) — though no evidence supports it.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) ledger-db disk_used_pct reached 100.0% in the 14:56–14:59Z bucket, before payment-service's first error at 15:00:26Z; the 180 s bucket resolution bounds the 100% crossing to no later than 14:59Z+180s.

timeline.event: ledger-db measured disk_used_pct is 96.58% — already near-full well before any deploy (F28).
ledger-db logs WARN "replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 33916 MB of WAL" — the disk-pressure origin, ~12 min before the v6.0.0 deploy (F11, F16).
payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, 'New UPI mandate flow', adds MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type) deployed by p.nair (F1, F13).
Retained WAL from the inactive slot has grown to 69518 MB (F11).
Measured ledger-db disk_used_pct pins at 100.0% (14:56–14:59Z bucket) — disk-full condition precedes the first application error (F28, F29).
Onset bucket: payment-service error_rate 0.2%→60.15%, order-service 0.2%→47.78%, settlement-service 0.28%→54.04% all in the same 15:00Z bucket; portfolio-service stays ~0.2% (F7, F24, F25, F26).
payment-service first ERROR: 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (F8).
order-service first error: 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device orderId=8ab6dc3a' — 16 s after payment-service (F27).
ledger-db PANICs: "could not write to file \"pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478\": No space left on device"; 'could not extend file "base/16402/2619"' at 15:01:39Z (F10).
Incident INC-012 reported (SEV-1) by on-call SRE; rollback initiated (F2).
payment-service v6.0.0 rolled back; error rates do not change (F1, F17).
Last available payment-service error — same 'No space left on device' pattern, still ~60% error rate; failure had not self-resolved by end of data (F12, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Free disk on ledger-db by dropping/recreating the stalled replication slot: run the slot-side remediation on 'analytics_cdc' (e.g. SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('analytics_cdc') after confirming it is not needed, then recreate if a consumer is restored) to release the ~77 GB of retained WAL.
recommended_actions.rationale: The retained WAL from the inactive slot is what filled ledger-db's disk; dropping the slot is the recorded resolution of the identical precedent HIST-114 ('Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert') and directly addresses the measured 100% disk condition.

recommended_actions.action: After the slot is dropped, verify ledger-db recovery: confirm disk_used_pct falls and stays below the 98% WARN threshold, confirm the PANIC'd postgres instance is accepting writes, then confirm payment-service, order-service and settlement-service error rates return to ~0.2% baseline — and that the pending ledger writes/backlog from the incident window drain.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback alone did not restore service (errors persisted at ~60% through 16:57:54Z); success must be verified on the ledger-db disk metric and on the co-writers' error rates, not assumed from the slot drop.

recommended_actions.action: Do not treat payment-service v6.0.0 as the fix target: keep the rollback but re-evaluate re-deploying v6.0.0 (MANDATE_HOLD path) only after ledger-db disk is healthy, and confirm post-redeploy that no mandate-specific error signature appears.
recommended_actions.rationale: Evidence rules out the deploy as origin — the resource trend started ~12 min before it, zero 'mandate' log matches exist, the error is a physical storage error, and rollback did not clear errors; the mandate flow should be re-validated rather than blamed.

recommended_actions.action: Add monitoring and alerting on replication-slot lag/inactivity and on ledger-db disk headroom (alert well before 90% on /var/lib/postgresql/data, plus an explicit slot-retained-WAL alert), and expose a WAL-size metric since ledger-db currently has none.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure was fully observable ~26 min before customer impact (98% at 14:38Z, 100% by 14:59Z) yet nothing paged; HIST-114's resolution explicitly included adding a slot-lag alert, and disk_used_pct is the only available signal today.

recommended_actions.action: Identify and take ownership of the 'analytics_cdc' slot consumer (or formally decommission it): enumerate the slot's client_addr/application_name on ledger-db, locate the process/pipeline consuming it, add it to the service inventory and to change management, and ensure it cannot stall silently.
recommended_actions.rationale: No platform component owns the slot (no analytics-service/CDC consumer in inventory, no dependency edge), so its inactivity has no identified actor and no change is recorded on 2026-06-01 — making the trigger structurally invisible and the incident unpreventable repeatable.

recommended_actions.action: Verify whether any other shared resource has an unowned/out-of-band consumer, and close the ownership/visibility gap: reconcile the service inventory against all replication slots and CDC sinks on platform-owned databases, and set retention/disk-cap policy on any slot so it cannot consume unbounded WAL.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root trigger lives outside the modelled inventory, so it appeared in neither deployment nor config-change records; without closing the visibility gap the same class of exhaustion can recur undetected.

recommended_actions.action: Re-examine, before closing the incident, why portfolio-service (a direct ledger-db writer) did not degrade while the other three writers did — check its ledger write path (retries, async buffering, or non-disk write path) and confirm it stayed healthy through end-of-window.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the one observation not explained by a pure shared-disk-exhaustion story and the truest remaining discriminator; understanding it both validates the scope claim and may reveal a resilience pattern worth adopting.

recommended_actions.action: Retrieve the evidence that was missed during this investigation: settlement-service's verbatim ledger-write error logs (log query timed out) and ledger-db host/volume telemetry (IOPS, filesystem, cpu_pct, connections_active) to exclude a storage-level fault co-manifesting with the disk fill.
recommended_actions.rationale: The shared-DB scope claim for settlement-service currently rests on metric correlation plus its status as a direct writer, and no host/volume/IOPS telemetry exists to fully exclude the storage-level alternative; retrieving this converts assumptions into facts for the post-incident review.

data_gaps: No metrics were ever queried for ledger-db's host/volume beyond disk_used_pct (cpu_pct, connections_active, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min were listed but never retrieved) and no IOPS/filesystem metrics exist — so a storage/volume-level fault (H3) cannot be fully excluded as a co-manifesting cause.

ledger-db exposes no WAL-size metric, so the '33916→77371 MB retained WAL' figures come from logs only and cannot be confirmed from a metric series; the disk_used_pct series corroborates only the disk-fill consequence, not the WAL attribution.

settlement-service's verbatim error logs were never retrieved (log query timed out 3x), so its participation rests on metric onset plus its status as a direct ledger-db writer, not on its own error text.

portfolio-service's health was not verified through the end of the window and no alternative error signature (latency/timeout) was tested for it; whether it is fully healthy or merely lacks the disk error is unconfirmed.

Tool budget was exhausted before the 15:10–16:59Z co-writer confirmation queries ran, so it is unverified whether order-service and settlement-service stayed elevated to end of data or whether portfolio-service degraded later.

payment-service request_rate and restarts metrics timed out after 3 attempts, so payment request volume stability and any restart coinciding with onset are unknown, and absolute failed-request counts cannot be computed.

No component in the inventory owns the 'analytics_cdc' slot and the slot consumer holds no telemetry or topology presence, so what inactivated it at ~14:34Z is structurally unanswerable with current tooling — this is the unexplained first cause behind the confirmed mechanism.

Historical search across two rounds produced no precedent for an incident involving a CDC/analytics consumer stalling, so the precedent supports the remediation (drop slot + slot-lag alert) but not the ownership/prevention model for the slot.

No schema-migration or ledger-service release records exist for 2026-06-01, so whether ledger-db's schema was ever changed to accept the MANDATE_HOLD entry type is unknown — a minor gap, since the observed failure mode is physical storage exhaustion, not a schema rejection.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that ledger-db's disk consumption was NOT predominantly retained WAL — e.g. a large non-WAL consumer (table/index bloat, runaway logging, a bulk load) that also fits the 96.58%→100% curve — would move the origin away from the inactive-slot mechanism.

A demonstration that ledger-db's disk was healthy at the application level while writers failed — i.e. writer-side errors with ledger-db disk_used_pct well below 98% — would break the causal chain and point to a write-path/connection-pool cause instead.

Evidence that the shared-DB scope claim is wrong — e.g. order-service and settlement-service on separate databases or not actually failing on ledger writes — would reduce H1 to a payment-service-local problem (H4) rather than a shared ledger-db exhaustion.

Recovery of the 'analytics_cdc' slot's state and retained-WAL volume before the fix, or proof that the slot was created/activated by an out-of-band change at ~14:34Z, would replace 'unexplained first cause' with a named trigger and could raise or restructure the ranking (H5).
Host/volume telemetry showing a hardware/filesystem failure (I/O errors, volume detach, IOPS collapse) on ledger-db would elevate H3 and change the fix from 'drop the slot' to a volume-level repair.

A reliable end-of-window series showing portfolio-service eventually degraded, or showing that its ledger writes go through a different (non-disk) path, would resolve the one observation that currently cuts against a pure shared-DB-fills-up story.

Evidence of a mandate/entry-type path reaching ledger-db and being rejected (e.g. 'mandate' log lines, schema/enum error text, or a schema-change record for MANDATE_HOLD) would revive H2, which is currently contradicted by the physical-storage error text and the zero 'mandate' matches.

findings.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred across ALL services in the 05:00–16:59Z window on 2026-06-01: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203), deployed 14:46:00Z by p.nair, 'New UPI mandate flow', adding 'mandate create/approve endpoints' and a 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD'; status is 'rolled_back' at 15:12:00Z.
No config or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service on 2026-06-01 in either the 14:00–15:20Z or the wider 05:00–16:59Z window (count: 0 both times).

payment-service does not depend on ledger-service for ledger writes: its outbound edges are payment-service -> ledger-db (kind 'db'), -> bank-partner-api (external), -> kafka (queue-produce), with api-gateway -> payment-service inbound.

ledger-db is a SHARED postgres component (owner platform, shared:true) written to directly by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service. So payment-service's ledger write path terminates in the shared ledger-db itself, and those three other services are neighbours that could affect it through that shared DB.

Historical search returned no precedent for a 'new entry type rejected' or schema-level rejection; the closest ledger-db write-failure precedent is HIST-114 (2025-04-18) 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL', symptoms 'write failures' / 'no space left on device', root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' — a resource-exhaustion cause, not a schema/entry-type cause.

No past incident's root cause matches 'new ledger entry type rejected'.

The payment-service error signature is uniformly ledger write failures, not mandate-flow-specific validation rejects: 59/59 ERROR logs in 14:30–15:20Z are the single pattern 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device', first at 15:00:26Z. In 15:30–16:59Z, 266 ERROR entries are the same pattern (only 2 WARN 'retrying idempotent request ... after connection reset' and 1 WARN 'GC pause'). No HTTP status codes or timeout/validation messages appear.

findings.statement: A search for logs containing 'mandate' on payment-service between 14:55Z and 15:20Z returned total_matched 0 (untruncated over the full 11:00Z–16:59Z data range), so no mandate-flow-specific error signature is observable in logs — the failure is generic to ledger writes, not isolated by the mandate path.

findings.statement: Re-confirmed: exactly ONE deployment (payment-service v6.0.0, dep-6203) across all services in 14:40–15:20Z; deployed 14:46:00Z, status 'rolled_back' at 15:12:00Z. No other service's deploy lines up with onset.
Re-confirmed: zero config/feature-flag changes for ANY service in 05:00–16:59Z on 2026-06-01 (count 0), ruling out a shared-config/flag change as the trigger.

ledger-db is a SHARED postgres (owner platform, shared:true) written to directly by FOUR services — order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service — so a ledger-db-tier degradation can hurt payment-service independently of any payment-service deploy.

Timeline mismatch: the shared ledger-db's disk/WAL exhaustion PRECEDES the v6.0.0 deploy. WAL retention from inactive slot 'analytics_cdc' was already 33916 MB at 14:34:05Z, disk hit 98% at 14:48:20Z, PANIC at 15:01:01Z — whereas v6.0.0 deployed 14:46:00Z and errors began 15:00:26Z. The resource trend starts ~12 min before the deploy, so it cannot be caused by v6.0.0.

Rollback did NOT clear the failure: v6.0.0 was rolled back at 15:12:00Z, yet payment-service errors continued at the same ~60% rate through the end of data (last error 16:57:54Z), still the identical ledger-db 'No space left on device' pattern. This supports that the deploy rollback alone is insufficient.

HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db 'disk full from retained WAL') was retrievable on retry and its recorded resolution is 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' with root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (category resource_exhaustion, symptoms 'no space left on device'/'write failures'). This is the same mechanism implicated by the inactive 'analytics_cdc' slot, so the precedent-backed fix is: drop/recreate the stalled slot (releasing retained WAL) plus add slot-lag/inactivity alerting.

findings.statement: No CDC/replication/analytics consumer exists anywhere in the platform inventory to own the 'analytics_cdc' slot. The full known_services list is api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider — there is no 'analytics-service' (lookup returned unknown service) and no CDC/warehouse component.

ledger-db's full dependency neighbourhood (both directions, depth 2) contains no analytics/CDC consumer: its inbound writers are order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service (all kind 'db'), plus api-gateway -> {order,portfolio,payment}-service http edges. So the slot consumer is not a modelled platform dependency and holds no telemetry/topology presence, meaning nothing about it can be observed changing around 14:30-14:34Z.

The 'no change exists around the slot's inactivity' argument cannot be extended by searching outside the 05:00-16:59Z window for deploys: I queried 00:00-05:00Z (count 0) and 13:00-14:40Z (count 0) and found zero deployments across all services in both, with partial:false. Combined with F1/F13 (only dep-6203 at 14:46Z in 05:00-16:59Z), the deployment record shows no change attributable to any CDC owner at any hour of 2026-06-01 — the gap is in ownership/visibility, not in the deployment ledger.

Config/feature-flag history for 13:00-15:00Z (the window containing the slot-inactivation onset at 14:34:05Z) is also empty: count 0, partial:false. So no flag or config change is recorded as having paused/gated any consumer at or before 14:32-14:34Z, in either the deployment or the flag plane.

Interpretation: H1's first cause (inactive slot retaining WAL) is only supported by the ledger-db-side resource signal, not by any identified consumer-side change. Because the slot has no owner in inventory and no modelled dependency edge, the upstream question 'did something change for the slot consumer at 14:30-14:34Z' is structurally unanswerable with current tooling — it is not evidence that nothing changed. The concrete, precedent-backed fix path remains slot-side: drop/recreate the 'analytics_cdc' slot to release retained WAL and add slot-lag/inactivity alerting (HIST-114), rather than a payment-service change.

findings.statement: ledger-db HAS a queryable disk metric: 'disk_used_pct' (unit %, 180 s buckets) is present in its available_metrics and returns a full, non-partial 51-point series. It is a MEASURED value, not inferred from logs: 96.58% at 14:20Z, and it is already at/above 98% from 14:38Z onward (98.21% @14:38Z, 99.08% @14:47Z, 99.72% @14:53Z, 99.95% @14:56Z, then pinned at 100.0% from 14:59Z through 15:08Z). Note the requested metric name 'disk_usage_pct' does not exist — correct name is 'disk_used_pct'.

First-origin test, metric-granularity caveat: ledger-db disk_used_pct reached 100.0% in the 14:56:00–14:59:00Z 3-min bucket, i.e. the measured disk-full condition exists BEFORE payment-service's 15:00:26Z first error. The metric bucket is 180 s, so this only bounds the 100% crossing to ≤14:59Z+180s — it is not finer than payment-service's second-level log timestamp, hence 'before 15:00:26Z' holds at bucket resolution but cannot be ordered to the second from this metric alone. H1 (shared-DB exhaustion) predicts all four writers fail on the same signature at the same time; the two non-payment writers that did fail (order-service 15:00:42Z, settlement-service 15:00:00Z bucket) began within ~16 s / the same bucket, consistent with H1.
